decision: Slice 4, ID-Q7/Q8: a matched re-send of profile, food, entries, settings, device status or activity merges into the stored record
alternative: A matched re-send replaces the stored record on every collection, as on 15.0.9 and as slice 4 already decided for treatments. Merge stays available through API v3 PATCH and socket dbUpdate, where a client asks for it.
restores: Every replace-becomes-merge cell: profile 61, entries 25, food 22, device status 13, settings 10, activity 5; re-sent over API v3 90, socket 36, in-process 10.
cost: Slice 4's reason applies unchanged: clients re-send whole records and clear a field by leaving it out, so under merge a cleared field stays set. Identifier-first matching, the duplicate avoidance and the unique index are unaffected. What is lost is the same as on 15.0.9: a field added on the site is dropped when the client re-sends its record. Clients found: AndroidAPS NSClientV3 settings, the web profile editor's saves.
recommendation: Strong candidate. Same rule as treatments, removes the cleared-field-stays-set risk, nothing in the identity work depends on merge.
status_note: Adopted: a matched re-send replaces on every collection, as for treatments; merge stays for API v3 PATCH and socket dbUpdate. Queued for 16.0.0.

decision: ID-Q6, slice 2: a placeholder, blank, numeric or over-long identifier is treated as absent on every path, API v3 included (WRITE_IDENTIFIER=lenient by default)
alternative: API v3 refuses a blank (whitespace-only) or numeric identifier with 400 by default, exactly as v15.0.9 did. Every other malformed identifier (placeholders such as "undefined", empty, over-long) stays accepted on API v3 with the identifier treated as absent; API v1, socket and in-process are unchanged.
restores: The 118 identifier-format cells where v15.0.9 refused a blank (78) or numeric (40) identifier. Corrected 2026-10-31: the card first counted 349, but 231 of those were placeholders v15.0.9 stored and only refused on a later re-send as an identity change; refusing them would be a new refusal, not a restoration.
cost: None to compatibility: no client can depend on acceptance that v15.0.9 refused. Refusing every malformed identifier on API v3 was measured against a strict run and would move at least 72 cells further from v15.0.9 (empty, JSON null and placeholders that v15.0.9 accepted), and a 400 can stall an uploader that only bounds retries on 404 (AndroidAPS, read). WRITE_IDENTIFIER=strict stays the opt-in broader refusal on API v3 and the socket.
recommendation: Strong candidate. Pure compatibility gain; check that no surveyed API v3 client sends such an identifier (none was found).
status_note: Adopted as option (i): refuse only blank and numeric on API v3 by default; no refusal v15.0.9 did not make. Queued for 16.0.0.

decision: ID-Q6: a placeholder identifier is not stored
alternative: Store the placeholder value as sent, but never match on it.
restores: The 1,387 cells whose only difference is that the placeholder value is no longer stored.
cost: The unique index on identifier would then refuse the second record carrying the same placeholder, which is the case two apps sharing 'undefined' hit. Excluding placeholder strings from a partial index is not expressible in MongoDB's partial filter. No surveyed client sends a placeholder, so the compatibility gain is on paper only.
status_note: Agreed: keep the decision; the placeholder value is not stored.

decision: WRITE_RESEND and per-client quirks: decided 2026-10-29, not built
alternative: Build WRITE_RESEND with a mode that gives 15.0.9's re-send behaviour per site or per registered client, plus a re-send counterpart to WRITE_DELETED_EDIT for revive after delete.
restores: Opt-in: d1 28 and d2 21 (stays deleted), c2 9 (socket re-send now written); b 402 only if a mode keeps adding a second record, which no one has asked for.
cost: Defaults unchanged, so the identity work is unaffected; the cost is building and testing one more setting. It gives an operator a way back without a revert, which today does not exist for any change.
recommendation: Worth building before the tag, or recording that 16.0.0 ships without a rollback switch.
status_note: Adopted: build WRITE_RESEND (and a re-send counterpart for deleted records) before the tag, as the opt-in way back. Queued for 16.0.0.

decision: Decision B and slice 6 (2026-10-31): a socket treatment re-send matched by identifier replaces; a device status re-send merges
alternative: A socket re-send that matches is acknowledged and nothing is written, as 15.0.9 kept the stored record.
cost: Edits over the socket go through dbUpdate, not a re-send, so few clients lose anything. Decided today for consistency with slice 4; both choices are defensible.
recommendation: Low stakes either way; leave as decided unless the re-send switch is built.
status_note: Not taken up: decision B (a socket treatment re-send matched by identifier replaces) stands.

decision: Identity first (b), new profile without the copied identifier (p), API v3 client _id refused (s, r; BF-170 on dev), the P4 pick (g), a time-key re-send after delete stored as new (d3)
alternative: Restoring any of these brings back the duplicate records, shared identifiers or collapsed records the identity work removes.
cost: Each is the substance of the agreement with the Loop maintainers or a prerequisite of the unique index. d3 differs only in whether the re-entered treatment is the old record or a new one; it shows either way.
status_note: Agreed: keep identity first, the profile copy rule, the API v3 client _id refusal, the P4 pick and d3.
